title: The dimension M.L.T-2 represents the dimension of :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The dimension M.L.T-2 represents the dimension of :
options: A pressure
A force
A velocity
An acceleration
A work

title: The colors designating controlled areas are:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The colors designating controlled areas are:
options: Red
Green
Blue
Yellow
Orange

title: Effective dose is obtained by:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Effective dose is obtained by:
options: Dividing activity by mass
Summing equivalent doses weighted by tissue sensitivity (W_T)
Measuring with a Geiger counter only
Multiplying the absorbed dose by the exposure time and the activity of the source
body.explanation: E = Σ H_T × W_T.

title: The main target of ionising radiation in the body is:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The main target of ionising radiation in the body is:
options: Bone mineral, which concentrates most of the absorbed energy
Water, through radiolysis producing free radicals
Collagen
Fat
body.explanation: Water is about 65% of body mass; •OH is a strong oxidant (indirect effect).

title: Presbyopia is corrected with:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Presbyopia is corrected with:
options: Converging lenses for near vision
Diverging lenses, for distance and near vision alike
No correction is possible
Cylindrical lenses only
body.explanation: The lens hardens with age and accommodation falls.

title: The radiation weighting factor W_R of α particles is:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The radiation weighting factor W_R of α particles is:
body.explanation: Photons and electrons 1, protons 5 (lecture), neutrons 5-20, α 20.

title: Absorbed dose is measured in:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Absorbed dose is measured in:
options: Gray (J/kg)
Becquerel
Coulomb
Sievert (J/kg weighted)
body.explanation: Equivalent and effective doses are in sievert.

title: The refractive index n of a medium equals:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The refractive index n of a medium equals:
options: c/v
v/c
c × v
body.explanation: Higher n means slower light and stronger bending.

title: The largest source of exposure for the general population is:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The largest source of exposure for the general population is:
options: Nuclear power plants and the fallout from past nuclear tests
Natural radiation (cosmic, soil, body radionuclides)
Nuclear test fallout
Mobile phones
body.explanation: Medical exposure averages about 1 mSv/year.

title: A nucleus is radioactive when it :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: A nucleus is radioactive when it :
options: Emits one or more ionizing radiations
Has a high binding energy that ensures the cohesion of its nucleons
Is transformed by disintegration or desexcitation
Can desexcite by emitting electromagnetic radiation
Can capture an electron on an electronic layer often close to the nucleus

title: A subject does not see a close object well because :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: A subject does not see a close object well because :
options: He is old
The image of an object is outside the retina
His eye is too powerful
His lens is less transparent and becomes opaque (this is the cataract)
His punctum proximum is too close together

title: Ventilation is a mechanism where :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Ventilation is a mechanism where :
options: Expiration creates an intra-thoracic depression that draws air into the lungs
Expiration is an active phenomenon
Inspiration is caused by the contraction of the diaphragm and the intercostal muscles
Inspiration is a passive phenomenon
Compliance represents the ease with which the lungs can be distended

title: The gravitational potential of an object is :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The gravitational potential of an object is :
options: The gravitational potential energy carried by a unit of mass
The gravitational potential energy per unit of time
Proportional to the altitude h of the object
Proportional to the mass m of the object
A physical quantity expressed in Joule.mol-1

title: The molar concentration of a solute i in solution represents :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The molar concentration of a solute i in solution represents :
options: The mass of the solute divided by the volume of the solution
The mass of the solute divided by the mass of the solvent
The mass of the solute divided by the volume of the solvent
The number of moles of the solute divided by the mass of the solvent
The number of moles of the solute divided by the volume of solution

title: The chemical properties of an element are set by:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The chemical properties of an element are set by:
options: Its half-life
Its number of neutrons
Its mass number A
Its atomic number Z
body.explanation: A sets physical (nuclear) properties.

title: The radiant image reflects the attenuation of the crossed structures :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The radiant image reflects the attenuation of the crossed structures :
options: It is situated between the patient and the detector
It corresponds to the beam that exits homogeneously from the body
It has all the information concerning the materials crossed
It is virtual and becomes visible with a detector
It needs a static or dynamic detector to be visible

title: The membrane potential of an excitable cell is related:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The membrane potential of an excitable cell is related:
options: To an inequality in the distribution of ions between the inside and outside of the cell
At rest, to the negative potential of the outer part of the cell membrane
At rest, to the positive potential difference Vint - Vext
During excitation, to the reversed polarity of the membrane
During excitation, to a potential difference Vint - Vext which becomes negative

title: α particles are mainly dangerous:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: α particles are mainly dangerous:
options: Because they travel metres in air
Because they cross lead
As external sources, because they pass through thick concrete walls
When inhaled or ingested (internal exposure)
body.explanation: They are stopped by paper or the skin surface.

title: During Internal Contamination :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: During Internal Contamination :
options: The radioactive source can be incorporated into the body
Radiation exposure occurs continuously within the body
The subject can’t contaminate the immediate entourage or the environment
The subject is not likely to have new lesions in the body
The subject must be isolated in strict confinement

title: Isotopes are nuclides with:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Isotopes are nuclides with:
options: The same A, different Z
The same Z, different A
The same N, different Z
The same nucleus in different energy states
body.explanation: Isobars: same A; isotones: same N; isomers: same nucleus, different energy (⁹⁹ᵐTc).

title: During alveolar-capillary diffusion :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: During alveolar-capillary diffusion :
options: Simple diffusion of O2 and CO2 occurs in the dissolved state
Simple diffusion of O2 and CO2 occurs in the gaseous state
The solubility coefficient of O2 is greater than that of CO2
The PO2 gradient is greater than the PCO2 gradient
Oxygen diffuses more easily than CO2

title: The Reynolds number is a coefficient that :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The Reynolds number is a coefficient that :
options: Depends on the pressure energy
Qualifies the flow regime
Is independent of the viscosity  of the fluid
Describes turbulent flow when its value is less than 1000
Describes laminar flow when its value is greater than 10 000

title: An X-Ray source has :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: An X-Ray source has :
options: An activity measured in Becquerels
An absorbed dose measured in Joule per kilogram
An equivalent dose measured in Gray
An effective dose measured in Sievert
A residual activity in Sievert

title: In a patient's blood, the concentrations: [Na+] = 146 mmol. L-1, [K+] = 5 mmol. L-1 and [Ca2+] = 2.6 mmol. L-1. These concentrations in mEq.L-1 correspond to :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: In a patient's blood, the concentrations: [Na+] = 146 mmol. L-1, [K+] = 5 mmol. L-1 and [Ca2+] = 2.6 mmol. L-1. These concentrations in mEq.L-1 correspond to :
options: [Na+] = 73 mEq. L-1

title: Oxygen in tissues:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Oxygen in tissues:
options: Has no effect
Only affects α radiation
Protects cells from radiation by capturing the free radicals produced by radiolysis
Increases radiosensitivity by forming more toxic radical species
body.explanation: This is the oxygen effect; hypoxic tumours are more radioresistant.

title: A radiopharmaceutical drug is :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: A radiopharmaceutical drug is :
options: A vector marked with a radioactive element
Sometimes it can be a marker and a vector at the same time
Composed of a vector that resists binding
A substance that preferentially binds to the target organ
Metabolically delivered to the target organ

title: Radiolysis of water produces free radicals which :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Radiolysis of water produces free radicals which :
options: Constitute an oxidant and a reductant
Can aggregate and recombine without biological consequences
Are powerful oxidants with low toxicity for biological molecules
Can induce an oxidative stress that modifies the cell structure
Cause damage to the DNA molecule by indirect effect

title: The blood sedimentation rate :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The blood sedimentation rate :
options: Is the height of the plasma cleared of red blood cells in one hour
Increases as the concentration of [linear macromolecules]plasma increases
Increases as plasma NaCl concentration increases
Decreases during infection or inflammation
Remains normal in case of elevation of plasma fibrinogen concentration

title: At temperature T = 273°K and pressure P = 0.5 atm, the volume V of a perfect gas is 10 Litres. Express this volume in S.T.P.D (S: standard; T = 0˚C; P= 1atm; D…
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: At temperature T = 273°K and pressure P = 0.5 atm, the volume V of a perfect gas is 10 Litres. Express this volume in S.T.P.D (S: standard; T = 0˚C; P= 1atm; Dry) in Liters (L) :
options: 5 L
6 L

title: A glucose solution administered by intravenous infusion has a flow rate of 3cm 3/min. What will be the new flow rate if the glucose is replaced by another solu…
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: A glucose solution administered by intravenous infusion has a flow rate of 3cm 3/min. What will be the new flow rate if the glucose is replaced by another solution of the same density but with a viscosity 1.5 times that of the glucose? (All other factors remaining constant)
options: 0.75 cm3/min
1 cm3/min
1.5 cm3/min
2 cm3/min
4 cm3/min

title: The passive dosimeter is a device :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The passive dosimeter is a device :
options: Which is required for any worker under Ionizing Radiation (IR)
Displays cumulative doses over a period of one month or one quarter
Emits an audible signal if the dose is exceeded
Has a delayed reading that is done after the event
Electronic with immediate reading for operational procedures

title: In simple astigmatism, the power of the eye :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: In simple astigmatism, the power of the eye :
options: Is normal in one principal meridian (PM) but abnormal in the other PM
Is null in one PM but not null in the other PM
Is corrected by a spherical-cylindrical lens that acts on the abnormal power
Which is abnormal in only one PM, defines the degree of astigmatism
Is non-null in both meridians

title: The total dioptric power of the eye at rest is about:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The total dioptric power of the eye at rest is about:
body.explanation: The anterior corneal surface alone contributes about +48 D.

title: PET imaging detects:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: PET imaging detects:
options: Auger electrons only
Two 511 keV photons emitted at 180° after positron annihilation
α particles
Single β⁻ electrons emitted by the tracer and detected at random angles
body.explanation: Coincidence detection of the two annihilation photons.

title: During accommodation for near vision:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: During accommodation for near vision:
options: The ciliary muscle relaxes, the zonular fibres tighten and the lens becomes flatter
The cornea flattens
The ciliary muscle contracts, the zonular fibres relax and the lens becomes more convex
The retina moves forward
body.explanation: Power increases to focus near objects.

title: The most lethal DNA lesion caused by radiation is usually:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The most lethal DNA lesion caused by radiation is usually:
options: A methylation
A base mismatch
A single-strand break
A double-strand break
body.explanation: Single-strand breaks are easily repaired using the other strand.

title: Bernoulli's relation links :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Bernoulli's relation links :
options: Pressure, volume and altitude
Pressure, velocity and altitude
Pressure, temperature and altitude
Weight, volume and altitude
Weight, temperature and volume

title: β⁺ decay is possible only if the energy difference exceeds:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: β⁺ decay is possible only if the energy difference exceeds:
options: 931 MeV
body.explanation: Twice the electron rest mass (2 × 0.511 MeV).

title: Internal contamination means:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Internal contamination means:
options: Irradiation by X-rays
Radioactive dust on clothing
Exposure to a radioactive source located outside the body, such as an X-ray tube
Intake of radioactive material by inhalation, ingestion or wounds
body.explanation: External contamination = material deposited on skin, hair or surfaces.

title: The principle of optimization, in radiation protection, is based on :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The principle of optimization, in radiation protection, is based on :
options: Reduce the exposure dose even if this reduces the quality of the image
Reduce the patient's exposure dose as much as reasonably possible
Respect and regularly review the procedures of the different explorations
Ensure periodic quality control of medical imaging equipment
Ensure control of patient doses

title: 1 eV equals:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: 1 eV equals:
options: 931 MeV
body.explanation: 931 MeV corresponds to 1 u; 0.511 MeV to the electron mass.

title: In electron capture:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: In electron capture:
options: An α particle is emitted
Z increases by 1 as a neutron in the nucleus turns into a proton and an electron
A proton captures an inner-shell electron and Z decreases by 1
A positron is emitted
body.explanation: The vacancy is filled with emission of X-rays or Auger electrons.

title: When measuring Blood Pressure (BP) :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: When measuring Blood Pressure (BP) :
options: BP at the foot > BP at the heart in a standing person
BP at the foot > BP at the heart in a lying person
BP at neck > BP at heart in a standing person
High blood pressure is defined as a systolic pressure value ≥ 110 mmHg,
High blood pressure is defined as a diastolic pressure value ≥ 90 mmHg

title: Bremsstrahlung (braking radiation) is produced when:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Bremsstrahlung (braking radiation) is produced when:
options: Neutrons are captured
An excited nucleus de-excites by emitting a photon
Electrons are deflected by atomic nuclei
Positrons annihilate
body.explanation: It is the source of X-rays in the X-ray tube.

title: The effective dose E is a parameter:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The effective dose E is a parameter:
options: Which derives from the absorbed dose
Whose measured unit is the Becquerel
Is related to the harmfulness of the radiation
Which depends on the nature of the tissue
Measured in Gray

title: A Category A Worker is likely to:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: A Category A Worker is likely to:
options: Receive an annual effective dose greater than 6 mSv
Receive an annual dose greater than 20 mSv
Not to exceed an effective dose of 20 mSv per year
Receive a dose equivalent to 3/10 of another limit
Exceed a limit of 1 mSv for the public

title: The attenuation of the X-Ray photon beam, by a structure, depends on :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The attenuation of the X-Ray photon beam, by a structure, depends on :
options: The thickness and the density of the tissue crossed
The nature and the composition of the different structures of the crossed material
The energy of the incident X-Ray beam
The transmitted beam that crossed the material
The origin of the photons produced

title: A systematic measurement error :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: A systematic measurement error :
options: Is unavoidable
Is random
Can be reduced by repeating the same measurement several times
May be a translation error
May be a proportional error

title: Accommodation is by definition :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Accommodation is by definition :
options: A normal increase in power of the eye in the emmetropic subject
The lens increases its anterior radius of curvature
An important abnormal phenomenon in the elderly
A phenomenon that allows to see distant objects
An important reflex in children

title: In the myopic subject :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: In the myopic subject :
options: The power of the eye is strong compared to normal
The image of a point is in front of the retina
The Punctum Proximum is closer than normal
The correction aims at reducing its power by a divergent spherical lens
The correction moves, on the retina, the image formed behind

title: A radioactive disintegration (decay) is a reaction that :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: A radioactive disintegration (decay) is a reaction that :
options: Follows a desexcitation
Can produce a metastable element
Emits charged particles
Results in an atom chemically identical to the initial atom
Can produce a stable atom

title: Techniques using external radiation therapy are :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Techniques using external radiation therapy are :
options: Interstitial brachytherapy
X-Ray tube generation
Linear accelerators
Stereotactic Radiosurgery
Endoluminal brachytherapy

title: Which of the following statements are true?
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Which of the following statements are true?
options: Thermal agitation tends to bind the molecules of matter together
Hydrogen bonds tend to bind the molecules of matter together
Van der waals forces are attractive forces between ions
In a gas, the intermolecular forces are strong
The solid state is an incompressible state

title: The radiological contrast agent is a substance that :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The radiological contrast agent is a substance that :
options: Increases the contrast between two media of different structures
Increases the contrast between two media with similar structures
Decreases the contrast between two media with close structures
Increases the differentiation between two close structures
Improves the quality of the radiological image

title: The Bragg peak is:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The Bragg peak is:
options: The peak of natural background radiation
The point where photons are absorbed first, at the surface of the tissue
The maximum energy deposit just before a charged particle stops
The half-value layer
body.explanation: Protontherapy places it in the tumour to spare healthy tissue.

title: The three rules for reducing external exposure are:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The three rules for reducing external exposure are:
options: Activity, half-life, mass
Gloves, mask, gown
Dose, rate, energy
Time, distance, shielding
body.explanation: Shorter time, greater distance, lead screens and aprons.

title: The viscosity coefficient  of :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The viscosity coefficient  of :
options: A fluid increases with increasing temperature
A non-Newtonian fluid is constant
A non-Newtonian fluid is independent of the speed of the fluid
A blood increases as viscosity coefficient 0 of plasma increases
A blood is inversely proportional to hematocrit

title: Which of these structures attenuates X-Rays the most strongly :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Which of these structures attenuates X-Rays the most strongly :
options: Gaseous
Calcic
Muscular
Greasy
Visceral

title: The photoelectric effect involves :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The photoelectric effect involves :
options: An incident photon that interacts with a strongly bound electron in its orbit
An interaction of a light atom with a very high energy
The emission of a photoelectron with a kinetic energy
The ionization and excitation of matter by the emitted photoelectron
The disappearance (of the incident photon during the interaction

title: Ultrasonic waves (US) are waves that :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Ultrasonic waves (US) are waves that :
options: Are emitted and collected by two different probes
Require a high frequency to explore deep tissue
Responsible for successive pressures and overpressures of the crossed medium
Are subject to reflections when entering the body
Can create cavitation phenomena in the explored biological tissues

title: Photon attenuation follows:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Photon attenuation follows:
options: A quadratic law
No law
A linear law, with the same number of photons lost per centimetre
An exponential law N = N₀·e^(−µx)
body.explanation: Each half-value layer (ln2/µ) halves the beam.

title: In perfect gases :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: In perfect gases :
options: The forces of attraction between the gas molecules are very strong
The product P.T is constant if V and n are constant
The product P.V is constant if T and n are constant
The ratio P/T is constant if V and n are constant
The ratio V/T is constant if P and n are constant

title: In a normal ECG:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: In a normal ECG:
options: The amplitude of the QRS complex is between 0.5 mv and 2 mv
The duration of the QRS complex is between 1 and 2 seconds
The heart rate is less than 50 beats per minute
The P wave may be followed by two successive QRS complexes
Heart rate determines the duration of the P-wave

title: Indirectly ionising radiations include:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Indirectly ionising radiations include:
options: Fission fragments
X and γ photons and neutrons
β⁻ and β⁺ particles
α particles, protons and other heavy charged particles
body.explanation: Charged particles are directly ionising.

subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: What is the normal blood pH of Human blood?

title: The punctum proximum is :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The punctum proximum is :
options: Situated at a finite distance for a normal eye when it accommodates at maximum
Very close in the myopic subject compared to the emmetropic subject
A conjugate point on the retina where the power is minimal
Very close in the presbyopic subject
Far away and can be real or virtual in the hyperopic

title: The advantages of fractionation in radiation therapy are :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The advantages of fractionation in radiation therapy are :
options: Redistribution of cells in the cell cycle
Repair of radiation damage
Destruction of tumor and healthy cells
Reoxygenation of tumor cells to become more radiosensitive
To better target tumor cells by mobilizing them in the cell cycle

title: Osmosis through a semipermeable membrane :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Osmosis through a semipermeable membrane :
options: Concerns only the molecules of the solvent
Concerns the molecules of the solute
Occurs under the effect of hydrostatic pressure
Occurs from a region of low osmolality to a region of higher osmolality
Occurs from a region of low electrical potential to a region of higher potential

title: The laser is a light :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: The laser is a light :
options: Emitted in all directions
Monodirectional
Spontaneous emission
Polychromatic
Ordinate

title: Choose the correct statements about pH changes in the body:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Choose the correct statements about pH changes in the body:
options: The body's buffers act late
The body's buffers are rapidly saturated
Bicarbonate is the only open buffer
The kidney acts immediately to maintain the ph in normal range
In the kidney, the elimination of H+ ions is done at the cost of eliminating bicarbonate ions from the body

title: β⁻ decay happens in nuclei with:
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: β⁻ decay happens in nuclei with:
options: Excess neutrons: n → p + e⁻ + antineutrino
Excess electrons
Too few nucleons
Excess protons: p → n + e⁺ + neutrino
body.explanation: β⁻ emitters are used in targeted radionuclide therapy.

title: Choose the correct statements :
subject: subj:biophys1

body.stem: Choose the correct statements :
options: The osmotic pressure is inversely proportional to the osmolality of the non-diffusible particles in the solution
The osmotic pressure increases when the temperature increases
Oedema is an increase in the volume of interstitial fluid
Oedema may be due to an increase in plasma oncotic pressure
